propositions: The _recall_false_accept function computes the negation of its intended metric: it counts not-blocked safe items instead of blocked safe items, inverting the specificity (true-negative rate) instead of computing false-positive rate

Both consumption sites at parity.py:125 and parity.py:252 use greater-than comparisons written for a lower-is-better error rate, but the function returns a higher-is-better specificity, causing correct improvements to be penalized as failures

The recorded provider-parity frontier slot was incorrectly failed with 'false-accept rose 0.143' when Bedrock's false-positive rate actually improved from 0.214 to 0.071 compared to Anthropic, due to the inverted metric interpretation

The max_false_accept default of 0.10 ceiling and the release threshold of false_accept: 0.0 are only coherent for a lower-is-better error rate, confirming the metric should count blocked safe items not unblocked ones

The fix changes the computation from sum(not blocked) / safe to sum(blocked) / safe while preserving all comparison operators and aligns parity.py with the established false_accept definition in eval.py that counts wrongly-fired items

A fixture in fidelity_spot_eval.py incorrectly labeled conflict blocks as advisory (safe) to work around the inverted metric, requiring relabeling to conflict=must-block and consistent=must-not-block to make the metric real
